title: The Deluxe on 35th and State, Chicago
summary: Garland starts at the Deluxe, upstairs on 35th and State, and describes the Blue Monday custom, the room and the competition with Billy Bottoms and Dreamland.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Uh-huh. And when you got there, where did you start to play in Chicago?

I went to Mabel Elaine, the show. Then we come back to Chicago, later on Chicago there, for a while, you understand. We got to go around different nightclubs, so they heard about the band. I went to work. Oh, you know, they got over there what they call Blue Mondays, Blue Wednesdays. Every nightclub has got a day. What is that? Yeah, the day, like, like they got just now, they call it a jam session. Well, all right, Blue Monday, all right, your place is closed. All your entertainers would go to the next club that day and do numbers, you know, sing or something, you know. You come in, anybody, you know, bands. All right, we went over to Deluxe, and everybody was crazy about me slapping their bass, you know. All right. Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Oh, yeah? In San Francisco? Yeah. It was upstairs street. But Dreamland was the one, and it was a pretty nice place. Across the street from there.
What part of Chicago was the Deluxe?

35th and State. It was upstairs over to old Panama. The Panama used to be right on the corner of 35th and State. A couple of doors over this way was the pool hall upstairs. Then next to it upstairs was the Deluxe.
Did they have stage shows too there? Flo shows or anything like that? Yeah. At the Deluxe?
There's not no floor shows. No, just floor girls sing on the floor because there wasn't nothing there for them to do. They danced right out there on the floor, you see?
